newsitem.title: EGYPT: Mubarak to discuss Jerusalem plan with Israeli PM.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak to discuss Jerusalem plan with Israeli PM.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Monday he hoped Israel's decision to build Jewish homes in Arab East Jerusalem would not unleash violence.

Netanyahu is to hold talks with Mubarak in Cairo on Wednesday, a week after Israel approved the building of a 6,500-unit settlement for Jews in East Jerusalem, outraging Palestinians and drawing international criticism.
Mubarak said he would tell Netanyahu that the Arab East Jerusalem settlement plan could complicate the fragile peace process.
"I hope the Israelis realise the complications which will be built upon this decision," he said.

"As to what we can do, will we declare war? No, nobody wants war, we are talking and creating dialogue with Israel. The Israeli prime minister is coming within two days. We will talk to him about it and discuss the future in the hope that they will realise the result of such actions," Mubarak said.
Asked if he would advise Netanyahu how to ease tension in the region, Mubarak said: "I am going to discuss this issue with him and will explain what the consequences will be in the near future".

"There is no problem between Egypt and Israel, the problem is the peace process. Our concern is peace and stability in this part of the world. Without stability, development is going to be very difficult. So we are going to exchange views and make him aware of what could happen if the process reached a collapse," he added.

Anger against Israeli settlement policy in Jerusalem has been mounting among Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip. The projects complete a circle of Jewish settlements around East Jerusalem which Israel began building after it captured the city in the 1967 Middle East war.
Sixty-one Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers died in gun battles after Netanyahu opened a tourist tunnel near Islamic holy shrines in Jerusalem in September.

Mubarak was speaking to reporters near the town of Toshka in the southern province of Aswan, where he went to see the first phase of the New Valley canal, an ambitious project that aims to pump water from Lake Nasser to the Western desert.
Egypt became the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel in 1979 and has since mediated in negotiations between the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours.

But relations between Egypt and Israel cooled significantly since the right-wing Netanyahu was elected prime minister last year. Cairo has been particularly critical of his policy of building or expanding settlements on occupied Arab land.
Israel says all of Jerusalem is its capital while Palestinians consider the Arab eastern part of the city the capital of a future Palestinian state.
Mubarak said on Thursday that Israel's decision to build the Jewish homes in East Jerusalem could worsen the already tense situation in the occupied territories.
He discussed the plan with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Saturday before the Palestinian leader headed to Washington to plead his case with U.S. officials.
"Arafat is going to state the position to tell them (U.S. officials) what the situation is. I am not sure he will be able to persuade them or not," Mubarak said.
"The problem is that building settlements without discussing the final status will complicate the whole process for the future," he added.
Under the terms of their interim peace deal, Palestinians and Israelis are to discuss thorny issues such as Jerusalem, Jewish settlements and the fate of refugees in final status talks.
The two sides held one round of these talks last year but have not resumed them since Netanyahu was elected.
